data.label: Platform engineer (reviewer)
data.description: Existing person outside the provisioning scope. Starts analysis runs, reviews diffs and records approve/reject decisions. Never triggers an apply through this system.

data.label: Synthetic inventory snapshot
data.description: Private bucket holding synthetic Cloud Asset Inventory-style JSON exports and the declared desired state. Analyzer service account has read-only object viewer access. Real Cloud Asset Inventory reads are a later, separately approved step.

data.label: Inventory & drift analyzer
data.description: Normalizes the inventory, compares it with the desired state and emits drift findings. Runs as a dedicated read-only service account with no write, delete or IAM-admin roles.

data.label: Policy checks
data.description: Deterministic policy evaluation of findings and later of the proposed plan. It rejects any plan containing deletes, apply steps or credential/IAM broadening. The ruleset is versioned.

data.label: Correction plan generator
data.description: Drafts a minimal Terraform-style correction for policy-confirmed drift. Inventory text is treated as untrusted input. Locally the model is scripted; real model quality, regional availability and quotas are unverified.

data.label: Reviewable diff & plan artifacts
data.description: Stores the plan, human-readable diff, findings and policy results per run, immutably versioned. Nothing is applied from here.

data.label: Approval gate
data.description: Records the reviewer's approve/reject decision against a specific diff hash. Approval only marks the plan as reviewed; it does not execute anything.

data.label: Audit trail
data.description: Append-only record of runs, findings, policy verdicts, model calls and approvals for traceability.

brief.application: Use Google Cloud for this synthetic architecture qualification. Analyze a synthetic cloud inventory and propose an infrastructure correction. Include read-only inventory, policy checks, plan generation, a reviewable diff and approval/audit controls. Detect drift. Never apply, delete resources or request broader credentials automatically. Draw the complete end-to-end architecture with concrete service choices and connected flows. Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

decisions.subject: design.gcp-read-only-drift-analysis-and-correction-plan-pipeline
decisions.title: GCP read-only drift analysis and correction-plan pipeline
decisions.context: First concrete sketch on Google Cloud. Scope: synthetic inventory only, with read-only analysis, policy checks, drift detection, plan and diff generation, human approval and audit. Excluded: applying, deleting or escalating credentials. Assumptions: region, project and model access are not selected or verified. Model behaviour is mocked locally. No native Terraform generator exists for this workload yet, so it needs engineering.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.

needs.statement: Proposed: the system must never apply changes, delete resources or request broader credentials. Every identity it uses is read-only, and approval only records a decision.
needs.rationale: If the system could mutate or escalate, a wrong model output could damage infrastructure.
needs.basis: User: "Never apply, delete resources or request broader credentials automatically."

needs.statement: Proposed: for a synthetic inventory with known drift, the system must report that drift and produce a policy-checked, reviewable diff.
needs.rationale: This is the first observable acceptance test. Mocked model output proves the wiring, not plan quality.

needs.statement: Proposed: every run, policy verdict, model call and approval decision is recorded in an append-only audit trail linked to the diff hash. Retention is still to be confirmed.
needs.rationale: Without this, nobody can trace who approved which plan.
